items.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: So that’s when I got Keter Betts, got June Bug, my buddy, and Louis Derry was on piano... And we went back and we had lines waiting to come in and see us.

ctx.x: Did you have a particular group of people in Tarrytown that you worked with steadily before the service?

What happened, when I was first playing the clarinet before Primo Rico asked my mother and father to get me a saxophone, also when I met Primo Rico I met this drummer, Holmes “June Bug” Lindsay, a black fella, and from there on we became brothers. We grew up together and we played in clubs all over town. There was a club in Tarrytown called Club Six. In fact I recorded it on my first album. And so I didn’t play clarinet there, I played the tenor. When I eventually played, we played clarinet, we called him Bug.…
I was just going to say, you played with Keter Betts?

items.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: So he brought a drummer from Tarrytown, and a piano player from New Rochelle and myself. And we came down there... We were right around the corner from the Howard Theater... so we spent thirteen weeks

ctx.x: It didn’t take you too long before you started playing out.

I was going out a year later. The next year I went down to Washington. A saxophone player from White Plains, Carmen Leggio, had been stationed down there in the service. And when he got out he used to go jam at this club. And the lady said, “if you can get a group together I’d like for you to come in.” So he brought a drummer from Tarrytown, and a piano player from New Rochelle and myself. And we came down there, you know, green. First time away from home, we got out and the whole bit. And we came in for four…

saxophone player named Rick Henderson called me in December to see if I could come down and do a month with him in January at a club down there, sort of like a supper club, and then Bostic came to town and heard me and asked me did I want to go with him, and that’s how it went on.
